newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan copper wire demand seen flat through 2000.
newsitem.headline: Japan copper wire demand seen flat through 2000.

text.p: Japan's demand for copper wire and cable is expected to remain flat through the year 2000, the Japanese Electric Wire and Cable Makers' Association said on Friday.

In its revised forecast for the fiscal year to March 1997, the association expected total shipments to rise a fractional 0.4 percent to 1,035,000 tonnes, with domestic demand seen rising 1.5 percent to 989,000 tonnes while exports were expected to slide 18.9 percent to 46,000 tonnes.
Continued growth in the construction sector would be partially offset by a slide in shipments to the communications, electric power and electric equipment sectors.

In its forecast for demand through 2000, the association predicted average annual growth in domestic shipments of 0.4 percent over the next five years, although total shipments would remain flat due to falling exports.
This year's trends in domestic demand were largely expected to continue, with strong gains in construction demand undermined by weakness in communications, automobiles and electric equipment.
In the last of these categories, consumer electronics were expected to show a particularly marked decline in shipments of 3.1 percent annually.
The projected decline in exports was blamed on increasing production capacity in other Asian nations. -- Tokyo Commodities Desk (81-3 3432 6179)
